newsitem.title: ITALY: Gelli, ex-leader of Italy's P2 lodge, arrested.
newsitem.headline: Gelli, ex-leader of Italy's P2 lodge, arrested.

text.p: Licio Gelli, the former grandmaster of the outlawed P2 masonic lodge, was arrested in central Italy on Thursday, Italian television reported.

The report said Gelli, whose lodge was at the centre of a political conspiracy scandal that brought down a government in 1981, had been arrested by police at his home in the Tuscan city of Arezzo and taken to local police headquarters.

Details were scarce but television and news agencies said a prison sentence of three years was pending against Gelli after the conclusion of a final appeal over sentences in a trial into the alleged illegal workings of P2, or Propaganda Due.
Gelli's lawyer, Michele Gentiloni, was quoted as saying he had asked for the immediate suspension of the warrant on the grounds that his client was not liable to serve the sentence.
"There has evidently been a material error," ANSA news agency quoted Gentiloni as saying.

The P2 lodge came to light in 1981 during an enquiry into banker Roberto Calvi, a lodge member who was found hanged in London the following year shortly before the spectacular collapse of his Banco Ambrosiano bank.

The lodge was found to have some 1,000 prominent members including top politicians, businessmen and military officers and its exposure brought down the Christian Democrat-led government of Arnaldo Forlani.
Gelli was arrested in 1983 in Switzerland, which conceded his extradition on condition that he would not be tried on perceived 'political' charges.

The reports said the Court of Cassation, Italy's highest court, recently confirmed an eight-year jail sentence on Gelli for illegal procurement of confidential documents. Five years of the sentence were suspended, leaving Gelli to serve three.
"Extradition for the offence of procurement of confidential documents for which he was sentenced...was neither requested (of Switzerland) nor granted," Gentiloni was quoted as saying.
"I have asked for the warrant to be suspended immediately," he said.

Investigations into P2 activities have repeatedly delved into allegations that the lodge conspired with right-wing extremists and the Mafia to destabilise the state through bombings and other acts of violence.
Conflicting findings by courts and parliamentary enquiries, however, have failed to resolve the case.
